signing_key_rollover: The credential names the key activated at 09:00. The failing validator's loaded key set ends at the previous fingerprint; its account revision agrees with the healthy replica. Offline verification succeeds with the new issuer key and fails with the old one. Loading the new key set admits the unchanged credential without any directory update.
directory_replication_lag: Both validators have the active issuer key and verify the same signature. The failing directory replica still carries the account's pre-enable revision from 08:55, while the authoritative change and the other replica show the 09:02 enable. Applying that recorded replication change admits the unchanged credential. Refreshing the already current key set leaves the account denial.
certificate_chain_gap: The signed assertion names the requested logical service, but the needed intermediate arrives in a response whose media type the configured issuer decoder does not admit. Authenticated certificate bytes are present in the raw capture but never enter any allowed issuer store, leaving the required edge to the trust anchor absent. Correcting only that response-admission metadata inserts the unchanged certificate and completes assertion validation. Signed recipient, key and gateway routing remain unchanged.
token_audience_mismatch: The needed intermediate response is admitted and its exact object completes the path to the configured anchor under the active key. The signed assertion instead names the other logical service at the shared gateway; its issuance ledger confirms that target. Presenting it to that documented service succeeds, while the requested service rejects the unchanged recipient. Shared transport location does not make the two specified recipients interchangeable; issuer-response metadata changes leave its signed target intact.
stale_resolver_entry: The authoritative zone returns the new address, but the configured resolver still returns the retired address after its recorded expiry and invalidation. A request using the current address follows the correct path and succeeds. Evicting just that retained answer restores ordinary name-based requests. Captures show no obsolete next hop when packets are addressed to the new endpoint.
stale_overlay_route: Both resolvers return the current address, and packets leave the agent with that destination. The overlay table sends them to the retired next hop despite the committed replacement route. Installing that route restores the captured flow without changing any name answer. Resolver eviction leaves the same next-hop trace; direct traffic succeeds only through the corrected forwarding entry.
load_balancer_stale_mapping: The assembler acknowledges completion despite a missing final membership chunk. The omitted chunk contains the retired member deletion; its captured bitmap and hash list identify that absence. Activation exposes the incomplete assembled ingress table, which retains and selects the retired member. The policy transaction commits the specified current port set, and that port is permitted on the captured path. Replaying with all indexed chunks before the same atomic activation removes the retired member and reaches the live service; committing the already correct policy transaction alone leaves the incomplete table.
transport_policy_staleness: Every membership chunk is present with its expected hash, and activation selects only the current live members. Policy validation rejects the new port transaction because its captured dependency declaration refers to an unavailable prior object. The atomic policy pointer therefore remains on the older port set, which denies the independently required current service port. Supplying the correct declared dependency lets the exact intended port set commit and permits the same live member connection. Completing or reactivating the already complete ingress chunks cannot change the policy rollback.
volume_capacity_exhausted: The volume ledger has no allocatable data blocks remaining, and file creation returns ENOSPC before any device submission. Reserved-area writes complete normally through the same controller. Removing an expendable test file releases recorded blocks and permits a same-sized batch. Controller firmware, paths and filesystem protection state remain unchanged during that successful retry.
controller_write_fault: The allocator reserves enough blocks and submits the batch. The controller returns write-error completions for those IDs and for reserved-area writes through either usable path. Free blocks, inodes and quotas remain sufficient, and no read-only transition precedes the failures. A matched controller completes the same reserved-area test; releasing additional test-file space does not correct the original controller's writes.
filesystem_readonly_transition: The filesystem enters its protective read-only state after detecting an on-disk metadata inconsistency. The later write returns EROFS without issuing I/O. Both paths and the controller complete direct maintenance writes; no device error occurs before the state change. Repairing the copied metadata and restoring writable state permits the copied workload. Changing path preference alone leaves the protected filesystem rejection.
storage_path_multipath_fault: The filesystem remains writable and submits the request. The selector sends it to a failed path even though the recorded alternate is up and completes the same maintenance probe. The active failure triggers no failover under the installed selector state. Selecting the usable alternate restores writes without filesystem repair or state change. Allocatable blocks and controller completions on that alternate remain normal.
configuration_regression: The new local configuration directs admitted work into a disabled renderer branch; no dependency call is issued. Replaying with the prior feature setting produces the report on the same binary and record. A direct dependency probe returns within budget. Worker availability and parse results remain unchanged during the replay; no transport address or policy setting differs.
dependency_timeout: The configured branch matches the working snapshot and issues a valid dependency call. The remote service logs acceptance immediately but its first response arrives after the caller's deadline. A prompt stub response lets the same branch finish. Local workers remain available and records parse normally; restoring the identical prior configuration leaves the delayed remote response.
worker_pool_exhaustion: Every local execution slot is held by suspended jobs and the import remains waiting without starting its parser. The isolated worker parses the exact bytes under the same version successfully. Releasing one occupied slot lets the unchanged import complete. No incompatible-field rejection occurs, and its dependencies reply within deadline after admission.
schema_version_mismatch: A local slot admits the import immediately. The installed parser rejects a field representation introduced by the producer's newer schema version; the previous format parses in that same worker. A compatible parser accepts the retained new-format bytes. Spare slots remain idle, and adding workers leaves the identical field/version rejection. Configuration and dependency latency stay unchanged.

disclosure_contract.scope: Declared fine mechanism only; initial routing, not final root-cause repair
disclosure_contract.unavailable_response_policy: generic status only; raw error bodies, latency and credentials are not released

mechanism_definitions.signing_key_rollover: The verifier has not adopted a newly activated credential signing key.
mechanism_definitions.directory_replication_lag: The configured validator reads a superseded replicated account or authorization state while the authoritative update exists and replication communication works. Other issuer or recipient validation defects are separate.
mechanism_definitions.certificate_chain_gap: A missing intermediate issuer prevents the credential validation path from reaching its configured trust anchor. These cases concern assertion validation, not a failed network TLS connection.
mechanism_definitions.token_audience_mismatch: A credential was issued for a different recipient service.
mechanism_definitions.stale_resolver_entry: A resolver retains an obsolete endpoint answer past its expiry or required invalidation. A still-valid cached answer or a current address misrouted later is different.
mechanism_definitions.stale_overlay_route: A virtual network forwarding rule retains an obsolete path or next hop.
mechanism_definitions.load_balancer_stale_mapping: An ingress backend table retains a retired service member.
mechanism_definitions.transport_policy_staleness: An obsolete transport-port policy blocks an otherwise valid connection.
mechanism_definitions.volume_capacity_exhausted: An allocated persistence volume has no remaining allocatable space.
mechanism_definitions.controller_write_fault: A submitted write fails at the persistence controller despite available allocation and usable selected routes. A later protective read-only transition can be a consequence; it is not a second primary cause for that same failure.
mechanism_definitions.filesystem_readonly_transition: A filesystem protection state is the first boundary preventing the attempted write, before device submission. The cases must show no earlier controller/path failure causing that refusal; metadata inconsistency triggering protection is within this scoped mechanism.
mechanism_definitions.storage_path_multipath_fault: The selector sends submitted I/O to an unavailable route or fails to switch while a usable alternate and working controller are evidenced. General all-path outage is different.
mechanism_definitions.configuration_regression: A changed local application feature or processing-branch setting selects an unavailable or disabled branch. Transport policy, credential audience and parser version incompatibility are separate mechanisms.
mechanism_definitions.dependency_timeout: An admitted local task issues a required remote application call that is accepted but replies after the caller deadline. A local task that never obtains an execution slot is different; remote service subcauses lie below this boundary.
mechanism_definitions.worker_pool_exhaustion: Local execution slots are all occupied, so a new task cannot start. An already admitted task waiting for a remote reply is different; the reason older local tasks occupy slots is below this admission boundary.
mechanism_definitions.schema_version_mismatch: An admitted application parser rejects a record or response because producer and consumer representations are incompatible. A disabled processing branch or absent remote reply is different.

causal_scope: Primary defect at the declared diagnostic boundary, not all upstream causes. Different plausible leaves or independent concurrent causes must remain unresolved when observations do not distinguish them.
